24584-man-overboard.title: Man Overboard!
24584-man-overboard.creator: F. Marion Crawford
24584-man-overboard.description: A book by F. Marion Crawford. nk I remember seeing a man come back when he was once fairly gone more than two or three times in all my life, though we have often picked up the life-buoy, and sometimes the fellow's cap. Stokers and passengers jump over; I never knew a sailor to do that, drunk or sober. Yes, they say it has happened on hard ships, but I never knew a case myself.

arxiv-2103-02917.title: MP Twitter Engagement and Abuse Post-first COVID-19 Lockdown in the UK: White Paper
arxiv-2103-02917.creator: TFTracie Farrell, MBMehmet Bakir, KLKalina Bontcheva
arxiv-2103-02917.description: Abstract The UK has had a volatile political environment for some years now, with Brexit and leadership crises marking the past five years. With this work, we wanted to understand more about how the global health emergency, COVID-19, influences the amount, type or topics of abuse that UK politicians receive when engaging with the public.

arxiv-2104-12083.title: Minimum Orbital Periods of H-Rich Bodies Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2104-12083.creator: S. Rappaport, A. Vanderburg, J. Schwab, L. Nelson
arxiv-2104-12083.description: Abstract In this work we derive the minimum allowed orbital periods of H-rich bodies ranging in mass from Saturn’s mass to 1 M ⊙ M_{\odot} , emphasizing gas giants and brown dwarfs over the range 0.0003 − 0.074 ​ M ⊙ 0.0003-0.074\,M_{\odot} .

arxiv-2208-02698.title: Dark Matter and Neutrino Masses in a Portalino-like Model
arxiv-2208-02698.creator: Dugald Hepburn, and Stephen M. West
arxiv-2208-02698.description: Abstract We explore a Portalino-like model of dark matter and neutrino masses in which right-handed neutrino fields connect gauge neutral operators from the Standard Model and Hidden Sector. Neutrino masses are generated via a seesaw-like mechanism that can explain the light active neutrino masses. The model includes a “Portalino” state that connects the two sectors via the neutrino portal.

arxiv-2307-05657.title: Mixed-Precision Quantization with Cross-Layer Dependencies
arxiv-2307-05657.creator: Zihao Deng, Xin Wang, Sayeh Sharify, Michael Orshansky
arxiv-2307-05657.description: Abstract Quantization is commonly used to compress and accelerate deep neural networks. Quantization assigning the same bit-width to all layers leads to large accuracy degradation at low precision and is wasteful at high precision settings. Mixed-precision quantization (MPQ) assigns varied bit-widths to layers to optimize the accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

arxiv-2407-00514.title: Combining Classical and Probabilistic Independence Reasoning to Verify the Security of Oblivious Algorithms (Extended Version)
arxiv-2407-00514.creator: Pengbo Yan(✉), Toby Murray, Olga Ohrimenko, Van-Thuan Pham, Robert Sison
arxiv-2407-00514.description: Abstract We consider the problem of how to verify the security of probabilistic oblivious algorithms formally and systematically. Unfortunately, prior program logics fail to support a number of complexities that feature in the semantics and invariant needed to verify the security of many practical probabilistic oblivious algorithms.

arxiv-2408-06915.title: On the KG-constrained Bekenstein’s disformal transformation of the Einstein-Hilbert action
arxiv-2408-06915.creator: Allan L. Alinea and Joshwa DJ. Ordoñez
arxiv-2408-06915.description: Abstract Motivated by an inclination for symmetry and possible extension of the General Theory of Relativity within the framework of Scalar Theory, we investigate the Bekenstein’s disformal transformation of the Einstein-Hilbert action. Owing to the complicated combinations of second order metric derivatives encoded in the Ricci scalar of the action, such a transformation yields an unwieldy expression.

arxiv-2409-14759.title: VLM’s Eye Examination: Instruct and Inspect Visual Competency of Vision Language Models
arxiv-2409-14759.creator: Nam Hyeon-Woo hyeonw.nam@postech.ac.kr, Moon Ye-Bin ybmoon@postech.ac.kr, Wonseok Choi wonseok.c@postech.ac.kr, Lee Hyun hyunlee@postech.ac.kr, Tae-Hyun Oh taehyun@postech.ac.kr
arxiv-2409-14759.description: Abstract Vision language models (VLMs) have shown promising reasoning capabilities across various benchmarks; however, our understanding of their visual perception remains limited. In this work, we propose an eye examination process to investigate how a VLM perceives images, specifically focusing on key elements of visual recognition, from primitive color and shape to semantic levels.

arxiv-2409-17848.title: Interplay of metallicity, ferroelectricity and layer charges in SmNiO 3 ​ / BaTiO 3 \text{SmNiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}}\text{/}\text{BaTiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} superlattices
arxiv-2409-17848.creator: Edith Simmen, Nicola A. Spaldin
arxiv-2409-17848.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Edith Simmen, Nicola A. Spaldin. Using density-functional theory, we demonstrate that the formal layer charges of the metallic samarium nickelate electrode influence the spontaneous ferroelectric polarization of the barium titanate in SmNiO 3 ​ / BaTiO 3 \text{SmNiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}}\text{/}\text{BaTiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} capacitors. We find that, despite the metallic screening of SmNiO 3 \text{SmNiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} , the spontaneous polarization of BaTiO 3 \text{BaTiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} always aligns with the layer polarization of the SmNiO 3 \text{SmNiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{3}}} formal charges.

Part of the
arxiv-2506-12218.creator: Samuel Rey, Hamed Ajorlou, and Gonzalo Mateos
arxiv-2506-12218.description: Abstract Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) are central to science and engineering applications including causal inference, scheduling, and neural architecture search. In this work, we introduce the DAG Convolutional Network (DCN), a novel graph neural network (GNN) architecture designed specifically for convolutional learning from signals supported on DAGs.

pmc-12567263.title: Research into the Influence of Volume Fraction on the Bending Properties of Selected Thermoplastic Cellular Structures from a Mechanical and Energy Absorption Perspective
pmc-12567263.creator: Katarina Monkova, Peter Pavol Monka, Damir Godec, Monika Torokova, Vineet Kumar, Md Najib Alam
pmc-12567263.description: The aim of the manuscript is to study the effect of volume fraction on the bending properties of selected thermoplastic cellular structures (Primitive, Diamond, and Gyroid) from a mechanical and energy absorption perspective, with a view to their promising prospects and use not only for bumpers, but also for various vehicle and aircraft components, or other applications.

pmc-13121130.title: Therapeutic progress in the management of triplane fractures in adolescents
pmc-13121130.creator: Qiqi Wei, Wenlong Ma, Guangshui Lv, Fanglong Zheng, Cheng Jing, Yanbo Guo
pmc-13121130.description: The triplane fracture is a complex, idiosyncratic, and relatively rare type of specialized fracture of adolescents. The fracture type of triplane fractures is determined by the mechanism of injury and the degree of closure of the epiphyseal plate. The absence of a universally accepted framework for categorizing triplane fractures increase the likelihood of being underdiagnosed.

pmc-13391827.title: Heterogeneity and plasticity of tumor-associated macrophages in oral squamous cell carcinoma: implications for diagnosis and tumor microenvironment characterization
pmc-13391827.creator: Manuel Olmos, Tobias Möst, Christopher-Philipp Nobis, Nicolai Oetter, Linus Winter, Christoph Vogl, Marco Kesting, Jutta Ries
pmc-13391827.description: BackgroundOral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the predominant histological subtype of oral cavity cancers, with a 5-year survival rate of approximately 50%. The tumour microenvironment, particularly macrophage infiltration and polarization, plays a critical role in tumour progression and patient prognosis.

pmc-13445562.title: Understanding Nurses’ Perceptions of Patient‐Centered Care: The Influence of Interprofessional Collaboration
pmc-13445562.creator: Trang Thi Thuy Ho, Binh Thi Diem Vo, Thao Thi Phuong Hoang
pmc-13445562.description: BackgroundPatient‐centered care and interprofessional collaboration are fundamental to high‐quality healthcare. This study investigated nurses’ perceptions of patient‐centered care and interprofessional collaboration and its factors.MethodsA descriptive cross‐sectional survey was conducted. A total of 320 nurses from multiple hospitals in Vietnam participated in the study.

pmc-13512389.title: Association Between Cachexia Defined by the Asian Working Group for Cachexia Criteria and One-Year Post-Discharge Mortality in Older Adults with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
pmc-13512389.creator: Daisuke Suzuki, Toshimi Sato, Yuichiro Sasamoto, Shun Monoe, Keita Kaneko, Shinichiro Morishita
pmc-13512389.description: Background: Cachexia is a well-known clinically important condition in older adults with heart failure, but evidence regarding cachexia defined by the Asian Working Group for Cachexia (AWGC) criteria in those with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) remains limited. Methods: This prospective observational study included 78 patients aged 65 years or older who were hospitalized for ADHF.

pmc-13581316.title: Validity and Reliability of the Korean Version of the Supportive Care Needs Scale for Tuberculosis Patients
pmc-13581316.creator: Hyemi Ha, Jeong Won Han
pmc-13581316.description: AimTo develop a culturally appropriate Korean version of the Supportive Care Needs Scale for Patients with Tuberculosis and to rigorously evaluate its validity and reliability for use as a standardized assessment tool.DesignA cross‐sectional study.MethodsThe original tool underwent standardized translation and cultural adaptation, followed by expert review and pilot testing to finalize the Korean version.
